note: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) describe an NFU1 phenotype spectrum ranging from early-onset pure to complex HSP, with progressive or relapsing neurological decompensation.

evidence.text: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) reported 19 individuals with bi-allelic NFU1 missense variants exhibiting a spectrum from early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, often accompanied by episodic neurological decompensation.

source.title: Phenotypic continuum of NFU1-related disorders
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: We report 19 affected individuals from 10 independent families with ultra-rare bi-allelic NFU1 missense variants associated with a spectrum of early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotype with a longer survival (16/19) on one end and neurodevelopmental delay with severe hypotonia (3/19) on the other.

numbers.metric: patients presenting on HSP spectrum with longer survival

evidence.text: Mahmoud et al. (2025) note that NFU1 variants encompass a clinical spectrum starting initially as milder pure HSP before progressing.
